A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same dense-voxel streaming framework, renamed from DuOcc to StreamOcc. All pages, including equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original occupancy-prediction results, component ablations, detection evaluations, and computational measurements on Occ3D-nuScenes and SurroundOcc.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds a query-selection ablation and detector visualizations.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 and Eq. (5) revise the stated temporal fusion from adding current and refined historical features to concatenating them followed by Conv1D. The refinement attention, query aggregation, auxiliary supervision, and loss weights otherwise remain substantially unchanged; their renaming does not establish new components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Occ3D-nuScenes and SurroundOcc occupancy tasks and associated detection outputs. Added analyses remain within existing coverage; distant, overlapping, occluded, and rainy-scene examples were already represented in v2.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GEOcc, ALOcc, STCOcc, ViewFormer, and ALOcc-mini while removing SurroundOcc. Table 2 replaces BEVFormer with QuadricFormer, and Table 3 adds FB-OCC and ALOcc-mini. GSD-Occ disappears from the per-class comparison in Table 4 and is replaced by ALOcc-mini in Figure 4. These substantially revise comparator coverage.

E3.justification: v3 extends dynamic-object mIoU reporting to the main benchmark comparisons and introduces controlled query-selection variants. The CVPR 2025 ProtoOcc row changes image size from 256×704 to 432×800. Added ALOcc and ViewFormer comparisons explicitly use reproduction without CBGS. The proposed model's stated training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a four-strategy query-selection ablation, and Figure S1 examines whether voxel features reduce detector false positives. Figure 4 revises the qualitative baseline comparison. Conversely, v2's separate FLOPs/parameter analysis is removed. Tables 4–7 and most supplementary qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: The result set expands through new comparator entries, dynamic-object scores, and Table S1. SurroundOcc results change from 33.4 IoU/23.0 mIoU to 33.8/23.4; GaussianFormer-2 changes from 30.4/19.7 to 31.7/20.8. FB-OCC's Table 1 mIoU changes from 37.5 to 39.1. The proposed method's Occ3D mIoU of 41.9, RayIoU of 41.1, and principal ablations remain unchanged. FLOPs/parameter results are removed. Table S1 reports confidence-only mIoU as 40.7, conflicting with 40.1 in its discussion.

T1.justification: Eq. (5) substantively changes the mathematical definition of temporal fusion from a sum to a learned projection of concatenated features. No theorems or proofs are added. Appendix B.1's standard IoU/RayIoU formulas explain metrics already used in v2.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly claims the first framework integrating streaming with dense voxel representations and foregrounds dynamic-object performance advantages. The central dual-aggregation and real-time accuracy claims remain. The earlier headline claim of over 40% memory reduction and concluding downstream joint-prediction claim are removed.

C2.justification: v3 adds a rationale connecting boundary-concentrated warping artifacts to geometry-guided residual correction and interprets the new selection and detector analyses. It removes the FLOPs/parameter-based efficiency discussion. The query-selection leakage warning and most explanations concerning occlusion and dynamic objects already appeared in v2.

D1.justification: v3 newly discloses training without CBGS and identifies visibility-mask usage and reproduced baselines in Table 1. It replaces the direct DuOcc repository link with a StreamOcc project-page link. Some decoder details, including explicit 3D deconvolution and Mask2Former-based auxiliary heads, disappear; most hyperparameters and loss weights are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including ALOcc, ViewFormer, STCOcc, QuadricFormer, and CBGS, while removing several earlier streaming and auxiliary-supervision references. Its positioning more explicitly contrasts dense voxel streaming with ViewFormer's compressed BEV representation. The underlying efficiency-versus-spatial-fidelity positioning remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and substantial method explanations are rewritten around dense voxel streaming. Terminology changes throughout, component ablations are consolidated into Section 4.4, qualitative analysis receives a separate section, and references move after the supplementary material. These constitute extensive narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Figure 1 is replaced by a challenge schematic and results chart; Figure 3 is redrawn, Figure 4 changes its comparison, and Figure 5 gains ground-truth displays. Benchmark tables gain columns, Table S1 and Figure S1 are added, and Table 8 is removed. Earlier supplementary Figures 6–10 are retained as S2–S6.

improvement.justification: More competitive baselines, clearer evaluation disclosures, dynamic-object comparisons, and the new query-selection ablation modestly strengthen support for the paper's claims. These benefits are tempered by removal of the FLOPs/parameter analysis and new reporting inconsistencies: the abstract reverses the benchmark-specific improvement margins, and the confidence-only ablation score differs between Table S1 and its discussion.
